items.title: Mike De Lay Interview, 1970-11-14
items.q: I played at a hall, I don't recall the name, it looked like it was on Calliope Street. Some people say, some people say, Calliope.

ctx.x: Can I ask you a question that I already know the answer to and John knows the answer to, and you know the answer to, and maybe the rest of the people who might read the book,

John knows the answer to, and what really constitutes Creole? Oh, well, no, I can't answer that. I can't. I can't answer that. You know why I can't? You see, I learned—so many things change when I grow up, so I can't answer that. You know what I'm saying why I can't answer that? It's because when I was small, I thought they had white Creoles, and I thought they had light colored Creoles, and I thought they had black Creoles. So, so you know I mixed up right there, let's face it. How the hell I'm going to ask for…
